▶ CLASSIFIER DESIGN: plan §41.1a (docs/plans/madc-repl-thonny-plan-2026-09-24.md), designed against the code. Two stages on the real front end. (1) Lexical: the lexer reports end-of-input causes (open comment / open #if group / trailing splice = INCOMPLETE; cut literal = INVALID), then DelimDepth checks balance. (2) Grammatical: the parser runs with an end-of-entry token appended; the first error decides (Julia, Python PEG): at the token = INCOMPLETE, elsewhere = INVALID. The optional final ';' (D11) lives in the one statement-terminator owner and applies only to entries with a value (expression / object declaration), so an Allman `int f(int a)` waits for its '{'. Verdicts: Complete, CompleteExtendable (top-level if without else), Incomplete, Invalid. Phase 0 test: classify_entry over a corpus, fresh Program per entry.
▶ LANDED this session (fix-what-you-find prerequisites; each its own commit with gcc/clang-oracled tests, Tier 1 + Tier 2 green, ledger rows):

  41aef5674: a literal cut by a new-line is "missing terminating \" character".
  cfb332e62: one escape decoder read_literal_escape (gate check-one-escape-decoder.sh). Silent wrong values fixed: L"\x1234" was 3 wchars, "\x041" lost a digit, a narrow UCN kept its spelling, \e was a backslash.
  aa2718a6c: multi-char constants fold gcc's way ('ab'=24930, was 97); '' is an error; #if '\xff' is signed.
  37c9dea0e: in C a character constant is int (sizeof('a')==4).
  49b7a5b19: if/switch init-statement and condition declarations get the statement's own scope (Program::StatementHeaderScope, also for-init/range-for). D18's bd3c56500 had REGRESSED tests/testifinit; D18's targeted tier missed it.
  c3a8153df: a file closes every #if it opens (cond_groups + refuse_open_conditional_groups; gcc's "unterminated #if").
  012f2dfce: a template instantiated mid-expression no longer moves the outer curToken/prevToken (finish_expression keeps the stop token; instantiate_fn_template_binding restores the pair).
  The whole JIT suite ran twice: 1648/0/0 (9 skipped) at 49b7a5b19, and 1659/0 with P1 applied. smaug_gate OK throughout.
▶ PARKED, NOT COMMITTED (P1: statements own their `;`). Patch + 7 tests + logs in tmp/repl/P1_wip/ (LOCAL ONLY by owner decision 2026-09-25: keep it local until finished, then commit it normally). Design: Program::StatementTerminator {None, Expression, Declaration, Jump}, stmt_terminator_owed set as the LAST act of parseExprStmt / parseDeclaration (wrapper over parse_declaration_body; not for a declarator-list head or a for-init) / parseKeyword (return break continue goto do throw, and typedef), paid by parseStatement through require_statement_terminator (gcc wording via token_before_phrase). Also drops TokenIF's ';'-skip before else, refuses a statement starting with ')' / ']', routes the identifier-as-keyword arms through parseExprStmt, and marks the for-init tail. It fixes `{ x = 3 }`, `int x = 3 }`, `break }`, `do {} while (0) return 0;`, `g(1));` and `);`, all accepted with exit 0 before. Whole JIT suite 1659/0 with it, BUT gxx-c++11 has 3 new failures: (a) cpp0x/initlist-new5.C `new Foo[1]{get_foo()};`: TokenNEW parses the array-new braced init as a COMPOUND STATEMENT (a latent bug the check exposes; fix TokenNEW to read a braced-init-list); (b) cpp0x/variadic121.C, a trailing-return `auto g(Ts...ts) -> typename foo<decltype(ts)...>::type {}` definition; (c) template/typedef15.C: a class-body typedef goes through parseKeyword and its owed Declaration LEAKS to the enclosing `struct ...;` statement, which then fails at the next `template`. Needed: scope the owed flag per statement (save/restore across nested parseStatement, not only reset at entry), or pay it only from constructs parseStatement dispatched directly.
▶ ALSO FOUND, OPEN (fix next, own commits): a dangling `else` (`if (x) x = 1;; else x = 2;`) is ACCEPTED silently, because TokenELSE has no parse and TokenKeyword::parse returns NULL (gcc: "'else' without a previous 'if'"); with P1 the if's ';'-skip is gone, so it must land with or after P1. u8"..." is "use of undeclared identifier 'u8'" in C17/C++17 (loud gap). UCN validity (C: \u0041 invalid) is not checked. 'é' (UTF-8 source, narrow char): gcc gives 50089 and clang errors, so it was left alone.

  015aefb97: a braced list on an ARRAY of class type initializes every element.
    - CirBuilder::class_array_list_init owns it: local arrays, global arrays, multi-dimensional rows, brace elision, value-init.

    - Program::apply_declaration_storage is one storage-class owner for every declaration arm. The ctor-args and auto arms had dropped `static`.
    - CirBuilder::emit_static_local_once uses __cxa_guard_acquire/release, with __cxa_guard_abort on the SJLJ unwind.
    - Block statics with dynamic initializers are supported.
    - A static `var` gets static storage (ObjStorage).
    - On macOS a __cxa_ import loads libc++.
    - Contract: thread-safe.
  534ba8a6e: a builtin operation on a `var` is refused (arithmetic, scalar conversion, truth test). Before, it ran on the carrier's long long[] storage and produced garbage with exit 0.
  e0b5c3e7a: `new T[n]{...}` initializes its elements. Before, the list was parsed as a compound statement after the expression. gxx pr52742 left the baseline.
  8b624a758: P1, statements own their `;`.
    - StatementTerminator and require_statement_terminator; StatementTerminatorScope covers statements, class bodies, and if/switch header declarations.
    - The TokenIF `;`-skip is removed, along with its two if-constexpr copies.
    - `'else' without a previous 'if'`.
    - The three gxx regressions: variadic121 and typedef15 are fixed by the class-body scope; initlist-new5 by e0b5c3e7a.
  572f1755f: a discarded if-constexpr branch ends where its statement does. skip_discarded_statement follows the statement grammar through DelimDepth. Before, it swallowed the next statement or bound a nested else.
  Whole JIT suite 1669/0 (9 skipped). Tier 2: gxx 1480 passed, 0 outside the baseline.

known_pre_existing_gaps: SCRIPT `value` IS NOT YET THE 32-BYTE madc_value STRUCT (recorded 2026-08-17, owner: not to be taken on now). Symptom: `value f()` returned BY VALUE emits `int f()` and silently returns nothing (exit 0, empty output) — func_def's return-type arm -> type_list -> append_type_specs has no dtARRAY case and falls through to int. That is why php::print_r returns madc::value & rather than madc::value. CORRECTED PREMISE: a C type DOES exist — madc_value (include/madc_api.h:52) is a tagged 32-byte aligned(16) struct, and madc::value merely CONTAINS it plus two unique_ptr members (32+8+8 = 48 = the emitted long long[6]); the opaque-buffer lowering exists because of those OWNING C++ members, not a missing type. MEASURED: _array/_object are private with no friends and all 40 refs are in ONE file (src/madc_value.cpp) — 12 mutations, 28 reads; the cell finalizer is already wired and called from generated code (cir_builder.cpp:25789/25797); the is_array_object sites would mostly RETIRE. HARD PART: the class deep-copies the containers while the cell path shares, so the migration needs copy-on-write at those 12 sites — a semantic change with its own oracled tests. Full write-up: docs/plans/2026-06-12-type-table-value-abi-design.md section 9. Sibling defect, also open: assigning to a `value &` PARAMETER is wrongly rejected ('assignment of incompatible value').

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.

MadArray/MadValue namespacing is an open API/ABI follow-up: moving the real C++ types to madc::array and madc::value would give PHP array helpers a normal namespace type surface, but compatibility aliases alone will not preserve old C++ mangled names.
